account: The National Foundation for Educational Research (NFER) ran a school-randomized trial in 2024, commissioned in December 2023 by the Education Endowment Foundation and the Hg Foundation. It involved 259 Year 7 and Year 8 science teachers from 68 state-funded secondary schools in England. Teachers in the ChatGPT group were asked to use ChatGPT, with an online guide, to prepare lessons and resources for ten weeks of the summer term, from April to July 2024; the other group was asked not to use any generative AI. Teachers used the free version of ChatGPT, which OpenAI updated during the trial. In weeks six to ten, a typical teacher in the ChatGPT group spent about 56.2 minutes a week on this preparation, against 81.5 minutes in the comparison group, a saving of 25.3 minutes or 31%, and the EEF gives this finding a high security rating. Teachers used ChatGPT mostly for one or two activities per lesson, such as quizzes or new activity ideas. An expert panel that did not know how the resources had been made reviewed resources from 30 teachers, 15 in each group, and found no evidence of a difference in quality. Teachers used ChatGPT less often as the trial went on, and the times came from teachers' own weekly diaries. NFER published the report on 12 December 2024.
